  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Duplication gate (production JS duplicated lines <= 1%, ratcheted)
        # Ratchet, not an absolute bar: a pinned set of production JS files
        # already exceeds 1% duplicated lines — pre-existing debt owned by the
        # gh-1244…gh-1250 dedup tickets (see duplication-baseline.json for the
        # current pinned set) — so the measurement's exit 2 is expected for
        # now. The baseline pins each over-threshold file with its measured
        # percentage and absolute duplicated-line count; the gate FAILS only
        # on a NEW over-threshold file or a pinned file that gained ABSOLUTE
        # duplicated lines (ci/duplicationRatchet.js) — a percentage shift
        # caused by file shrinkage passes and is logged as informational —
        # keeping the absolute 1% bar as the end state once the debt lands.
        # A crashed measurement (tool exit other than 0/2) never passes.
        # js/unit-tests/** stays excluded; the badge step below reparses the
        # same measurement for the README endpoint.
        run: |
          set +e
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" duplicates --threshold 1 --exclude "js/unit-tests/**" js ci > "$RUNNER_TEMP/dup-gate.txt" 2>&1
          code=$?
          set -e
          node ci/duplicationRatchet.js "$RUNNER_TEMP/dup-gate.txt" duplication-baseline.json "$code"

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e

The established pattern in production code: `if (typeof github_get_pr_review_threads !== 'function') return -1;` — bare typeof guards, one per entry point. Since smAgent.js is a huge file, per-call-site guards are fine there.

Given the duplication-gate constraint, my approach:

**mergeBackstop.js** gains ONE high-level caller wrapper that takes the caller-enumerated bridge bag:

```js
function runBackstopForPr(bridges, owner, name, job, prNumber, pr, say) { ... }
``

and bridgeIoOf is NOT needed — githubTools normalizes the bag. The caller enumerates its globals with typeof guards. To keep the caller-side code unique between mergeTrigger.js and mergeBot.js (duplication gate!), I'll structure them slightly differently but honestly the cleanest is: the caller-side enumeration is exactly the 7-line typeof-guard block... duplicated. Gate risk.

Hmm wait — let me reconsider. Which tokens does the duplication gate compare? crap4js duplicates — likely jscpd-style (token-based, min 50 tokens?). crap4dart.yaml says similarity gate min_shingles 50, jaccard 0.5, containment 0.85 — that's the SIMILARITY gate (file-level, "358 files scanned, no similar files"). The DUPLICATION gate is `crap4js duplicates --threshold 1` with ci/duplicationRatchet.js. The threshold 1 = 1% duplicated lines per file. Let me look at how ci/duplicationRatchet.js parses to understand what counts as duplicated lines and its granularity (per file pair?).

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Duplication gate (gh-1251): a second, independent gate fails PRs and main on
# NEW or GROWING JS duplication. The measurement is
# `crap4js duplicates --threshold 1 --exclude "js/unit-tests/**" js ci`; a
# pinned set of production files already exceeds 1% today (pre-existing debt

# `duplication` endpoint badge published from the same run.

content.text:
# Machine merge bot stub — event-driven fast path (frozen machine loop).
#
# Same freeze contract as machine-sm.yml: pinned immutable SHA of
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows; agents/CLI resolve from releases by
# vars.AGENTS_VERSION / vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION.
# The SM cron tick is best-effort (GitHub silently drops scheduled runs);
# this workflow reacts to EVENTS so approved green PRs merge within seconds.
# Idempotent against the SM: shared labels, first actor wins.
name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['Agent Docs']   # the only per-PR check this repo dispatches
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled, synchronize, edited]
  check_run:
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: machine-merge-bot
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  merge:
    # Label events only matter for the machine latches; other PR events
    # (synchronize/edited) always run — cheap and idempotent.
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      github.event.action != 'labeled' ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'ai_') ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'pr_approved')
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (same pin as machine-sm.yml — bump both together).
===
/**
 * Machine SM Agent — GitHub-issues machine-loop watchdog (JSRunner).
 *
 * The dark-factory loop over GitHub issues (dev → PR → CI → rework → AI
 * review → merge → close) relies on `labeled` events to wake the
 * ai-teammate workflow. Labels added with the workflow's own GITHUB_TOKEN
 * do NOT fire `labeled` events (GitHub rule), so every machine-added
 * label — agent:rework after red CI, pr_approved after an APPROVE verdict
 * — is a dead letter unless a human re-arms it (issue #116). This agent
 * is the safety net: a deterministic reconciler (no AI CLI, no LLM) that
 * runs on a short cron tick, reads the ACTUAL state of every
 * machine-managed issue (labels, linked PR, check rollup, merge state,
 * active workflow runs) and performs whatever step the state calls for —
 * dispatching legs directly via workflow_dispatch (GITHUB_TOKEN CAN
 * dispatch; only label events are mute), updating branches, merging
 * approved PRs, closing issues whose PRs merged.
 *
 * Concurrency contract: if any AI Teammate run is queued/in_progress the
 * agent idles for the whole tick (the cron re-fires soon — short ticks,
 * no long sleeps), so parallel runs finish before new legs start and the
 * per-issue concurrency group in ai-teammate.yml never cancels mid-flight
 * work. `maxConcurrentRuns` (default 1) relaxes this when the machine can
 * afford parallel legs.
 *
 * Configuration (override priority, sm-style):
 *   1. jobParams in agents/machine_sm.json (defaults)
 *   2. .dmtools/config.js `machineSm` section (project override)
 *      { machineSm: { dryRun: true, maxConcurrentRuns: 1, ... } }
 *   3. CLI JSON override (outer `params` wrapper — same quirk as sm):
 *      dmtools run agents/machine_sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"dryRun":true}}}'
===

/**
 * gh-1353 merge backstop before a squash-merge: counts unresolved
 * machine-owned >=IMPORTANT review threads; any count files ONE digest
 * issue and resolves each counted thread `defered: #digest`, then the
 * merge proceeds. Human-authored threads are never resolved — they are
 * listed `open (human)` and the merge follows branch protection as
 * before. Throws only on record-keeping failures (broken read, digest
 * filing) — processIssueItem/processOrphanPr isolation defers THAT merge.
 */
function backstopBeforeMerge(ctx, prNumber, pr) {
    mergeBackstop.runBackstopForPr(mergeBackstop.githubBridgeIo(),
        ctx.owner, ctx.name, ctx.job, prNumber, pr, ctx.say);
}

/**
 * The shared state machine (bash `case "$state"` parity). Returns
 * 'merged' | 'skipped'. `onMerged(mergedPrNumber)` performs the
 * post-merge label/comment bookkeeping for the caller's path.
 */

arguments.content:
### What changed
Wired the gh-1353 merge backstop (epic gh-1328 §4, part 4/4) into both merge funnels — `js/mergeTrigger.js` (the `pr_approved` sweep) and `js/sm/mergeBot.js` (the machine-SM merge path): before every squash-merge, unresolved **machine-owned** review threads with severity >= IMPORTANT (⚠️/🚨) are counted; any count files **ONE** `[debt] <PR title>` digest issue per PR and resolves each counted thread `defered: #<digest>`, then the merge proceeds. Human-authored threads are never resolved — they are listed `open (human)` in the digest.

### Key decisions
- `js/common/mergeBackstop.js` (from the prior WIP rounds, now wired + extended) stays a pure module — the two callers share one entry point, `runBackstopForPr(bridges, owner, name, job, prNumber, pr, say)`; `githubBridgeIo()` is the single place naming the engine's bridge tools (each `typeof`-guarded: an absent primitive = capability miss = skip, merge as today).
- Backstop is a **record, not a gate** — it never blocks on threads; a record-keeping failure (broken threads/comments read, digest-filing) throws through and only THAT merge defers (mergeTrigger: per-item isolation → `failed=1` job failure; mergeBot: said aloud, `acted 0`, queue keeps moving). Never merges undigested.
- Digest body opens with the review-debt-ledger machine marker → part-3 identity dedup holds (a repeated finding refreshes its entry; an already-open digest carrying this PR is reused, not re-filed).
- Deferral tag is the canonical `defered` spelling (reviewDispositions.TAGS / TAG_LINE_RE — the only spelling `parseDispositionTag` round-trips; the ticket's `deferred` variant would not be machine-parseable).
- Fails closed on identity: unconfigured `machineAuthor` → empty allowlist → nothing counts as machine-owned → clean replay, merge as today. Legacy third funnel (`smAgent.attemptMergeProbe`) intentionally untouched — epic scope is the machine loop.
- The resolve-then-ack order (gh-828 round 3), per-thread failure isolation, and fail-closed reads (#1319 pathology) are preserved from the module contract; `resolveThread` now rides the full `github_resolve_pr_thread` schema (workspace/repository/pullRequestId/threadId).

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_mergeBackstop.json   # 43 cases — counter, digest builder, wiring, io
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_mergeTrigger.json    # 56 — 6 new backstop-wiring replays (AC1/AC2/AC3)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_mergeBot.json        # 78 — 6 new backstop-wiring replays
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json             # full suite green
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  MT[mergeTrigger.runStateMachine] -->|decision=merge| W1[backstopBeforeMerge]
  MB[mergeBot.mergeApprovedHead] -->|approved+green+CLEAN| W2[backstopBeforeMerge]
  W1 --> RBP[mergeBackstop.runBackstopForPr]
  W2 --> RBP
  RBP --> CNT[classifyThreads — machine-owned >=⚠️]
  CNT -->|0 counted| MERGE[squash-merge as today]
  CNT -->|n counted| LED[review-debt ledger append + PR stamp]
  LED --> DIG[ONE digest issue /debt PR title/ + reuse probe]
  DIG --> RES[resolve each counted thread defered: #digest + ack]
  RES --> MERGE
  HUMAN[human threads] -->|never resolved| DIG2[digest lists open human]
  DIG2 --> MERGE
  FAIL[record-keeping failure] -->|throw| DEFER[that merge defers to the next tick]
```

</details>

### What changed
Wired the gh-1353 merge backstop (epic gh-1328 §4) into both merge funnels — `js/mergeTrigger.js` and `js/sm/mergeBot.js`: before every squash-merge, unresolved machine-owned review threads with severity >= IMPORTANT are counted; any count files ONE `[debt] <PR title>` digest issue per PR (severity, path:line, summary, thread permalink, review-run ref) and resolves each counted thread `defered: #<digest>`, then the merge proceeds. Human threads are never resolved — listed `open (human)`.

### Key decisions
- `js/common/mergeBackstop.js` stays a pure module; both callers share `runBackstopForPr(...)` + `githubBridgeIo()` (the single place naming the engine bridge tools — absent primitive = skip, merge as today).
- Record, not a gate: counted threads never block; a record-keeping failure (broken read, digest-filing) defers only THAT merge — mergeTrigger via per-item `failed` tally, mergeBot via a said-aloud defer (`acted 0`) — never merges undigested.
- Digest body opens with the review-debt-ledger machine marker → part-3 identity dedup (repeated finding refreshes; open digest carrying this PR is reused); deferral tag is the canonical `defered` spelling (the only one `parseDispositionTag` round-trips).
- Unconfigured `machineAuthor` → empty allowlist → clean replay, merge as today; legacy `smAgent.attemptMergeProbe` funnel untouched (epic scope is the machine loop).

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_mergeBackstop.json   # 43 — counter, digest builder, wiring, io

dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_mergeBot.json        # 78 — 6 new backstop-wiring replays
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json             # 8613 green
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  MT[mergeTrigger.runStateMachine] -->|merge| RBP[mergeBackstop.runBackstopForPr]
  MB[mergeBot.mergeApprovedHead] -->|approved green CLEAN| RBP
  RBP -->|0 counted| MERGE[squash-merge as today]
  RBP -->|n counted| DIG[ONE digest issue + ledger marker + PR stamp]
  DIG --> RES[resolve each defered: #digest + ack]
  RES --> MERGE
  HUMAN[human threads] -->|never resolved| DIG
  FAIL[record-keeping failure] --> DEFER[that merge defers to next tick]
```
